body.statement: Conditional on a proof of \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\) and hence on a proved uniform cutoff \(B_2(n)\), let \(G\) be any acyclic indegree-two mixed graph on \(n\) vertices. One exact call to \(DBI\) at degree \(B_2(n)\) terminates and returns yes with minimum-degree rational formulas if and only if \(G\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\). Its arithmetic complexity is \[O\!\left(B_2(n)n^5\{3B_2(n)n\}^{4\alpha_{\mathrm{alg}}B_2(n)^2\log(3B_2(n)n)}\right),\] and a no answer is accompanied by a complete exact bounded-search certificate rather than a timeout status. No unconditional total schedule is asserted before the frontier is proved.
body.justification: Once established, the frontier converts a promise search into a total formula-producing decision procedure on the stated class.
body.gap: Dörfler et al. give a total polynomial-space generic-identification decision without formulas, while Hollering, Misra, and Sturma return formulas only relative to a supplied cutoff.
body.consumer: Users of DegBoundedIdentifiability obtain an auditable stopping rule and an explicit worst-case resource bound for indegree-two graphs.
body.proof_tex:
This is a conditional compilation.  Assume the premise supplies constants and finite exceptional values for which \(B_2(n)\) is defined.  If \(n\geq n_0\), then
\[
 D_2(n)\leq C_2f_2(n)\leq\lceil C_2f_2(n)\rceil\leq B_2(n). \tag{9}
\]
If \(n<n_0\), the defining maximum for \(B_2(n)\) contains \(D_2(n)\), so (9) again holds with only its first and last terms.  Thus every \(G\in\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\) satisfies
\[
 ID_G\leq D_2(n)\leq B_2(n). \tag{10}
\]

For \(n\geq2\), the exact base cases and isolated-vertex padding give \(B_2(n)\geq D_2(n)\geq2\).  Apply the cited fixed-cutoff guarantee to \(d=B_2(n)\).  By (10), a rationally identifiable graph returns ``yes'', with the lowest-degree formulas found by the internal adaptive ordering.  Conversely, a ``yes'' output consists of graph-ideal certificates with denominators nonzero in the model coordinate ring.  Successively substituting them expresses every source coordinate rationally in \(s\), so \(\phi_G\) is generically birational onto its image.  Together with the stipulated acyclicity and indegree bound, this is exactly \(G\in\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\).  The case \(n=1\) is direct: the only source coordinate is \(\omega_{11}=s_{11}\), and the degree-one search terminates after this identity.

The algorithm at a fixed cutoff has finitely many weighted degrees, monomials, and exact row reductions.  Disabling a wall-clock timeout therefore leaves a terminating computation.  Substituting \(d=B_2(n)\) into the cited arithmetic bound gives exactly the displayed complexity.  If the search returns ``no'', retain, at every recursive state, the exact ranks showing that no remaining coordinate has a certificate at the cutoff.  This finite transcript certifies failure below \(B_2(n)\); combined with (10), it certifies nonmembership in the rationally identifiable class.  It is not a timeout assertion.  Every step used (9), so removing the frontier premise removes the uniform cutoff and this proof yields no unconditional schedule.
